method: Main cases were enumerated by loading tests/run.luau with registration recorded and execution suppressed. Every main spec was read and its cases were grouped into behavioral contracts. Each contract was classified against the candidate tests, api.md, the guides and src. Cited candidate case ids were checked against the candidate suite result.

liveEvidence.observed: On a reorderable VirtualList, a mouse press with 2 px of travel on the Move handle never reorders. It arms exactly one row for a move, and a second tap commits that move and ends it. A mouse drag past the threshold reorders once (row 2 to slot 3) and ends the move. A click on the row content activates it once. On the iPhone, a finger that travels on the row content pans the list and never reorders or activates. A finger held on the handle and then moved reorders once. The live run found that a tap on the handle was eaten by the UIDragDetector: DragStart began a move and DragEnd committed it unchanged. A detector release with less than 3 px of travel now arms the move, and the next one commits it (native_collections::Compose native collections::arms a move on a detector tap and commits it on the next tap, written to fail first).
